lesson.title: Finishing the Row and Meeting Colors: ਢ, ਣ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you learned ਟ, ਠ, ਡ. Today: finish that row with ਢ and ਣ, then start a new vocabulary set — colors (ਰੰਗ)!

ਢ and ਣ finish the tongue-curl row you started yesterday — ਢ is the breathier version of ਡ, and ਣ makes an 'n' sound with the same tongue-curl. Now for something new: ਰੰਗ means color. Learn your first three colors: ਲਾਲ (laal, red), ਪੀਲਾ (peela, yellow), and ਨੀਲਾ (neela, blue). Practice saying each color and pointing to something in that color nearby.
You finished a whole row of letters AND learned your first three colors! Tomorrow we'll learn numbers.

objectives: Recognize and name the letters ਢ and ਣ, completing the retroflex row
Learn and use three color words: ਲਾਲ (red), ਪੀਲਾ (yellow), ਨੀਲਾ (blue)
materialsNeeded: Objects of different colors around the room
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review ਟ, ਠ, ਡ from yesterday.
2. Introduce ਢ and ਣ, completing the row.
3. Introduce ਰੰਗ and the three color words, pointing to real objects of each color.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter and color word.
5. Close by finding one more object of each color together.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the three colors today, saving ਢ/ਣ practice for tomorrow's review
Ready for more: ask the child to name an object of each color from memory, without looking around first
Every Gurmukhi word used in this lesson was checked against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing, recognition, and vocabulary activity — check that the child can name ਢ and ਣ, and correctly use ਲਾਲ, ਪੀਲਾ, and ਨੀਲਾ for real objects.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Completes the retroflex row (ਟਠਡਢਣ) from the Painti Akhari sequence while introducing genuinely new, practical vocabulary (colors) — a real Grade 1 Punjabi curriculum goal beyond the alphabet alone.

worksheet.title: Finishing the Row and Meeting Colors

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter or word, say it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
